Lek Dat Type เหล็กดัดไทป์ — A typeface inspired by decorative ironwork

Exploring metal grilles across local communities revealed their role beyond decoration and security. A photography shop, for example, incorporated a camera shape into its grille to communicate its business while maintaining the character of the building.

If ironwork can tell us what a place does, could it also speak through letterforms? From shapes that express a place’s identity to lines that form letters.

Lek Dat Type translates the lines, rhythms, and bends of decorative metalwork into letterforms, bringing a familiar feature of local communities into a new form of visual communication.

Specimen signs: ติดต่อป้านี (contact Auntie Nee), หยุดทุกวันพุธ (closed every Wednesday), ห้ามจอด (no parking).

Designer : Ammily Prain
